# Translation of Sumerian Text

This appears to be a cosmogonic/mythological text, possibly related to the creation narrative and the gods' labors. Here is my translation:

1. In those days of old, when heaven and earth had been **fashioned**,
2. In those nights of old, when heaven and earth had been **fashioned**,
3. In those **years** of old, when fates had been **decreed**,
4. When the **Anunna** gods had been born,
5. When the goddess **Ama-dinana** had been taken for lordship(?),
6. When the goddess **Ama-dinana** had been distributed throughout heaven and earth,
7. When the goddess **Ama-dinana** [...] had multiplied and given birth,
8. When the gods' food rations had been bound to their dwelling(?),
9. The innumerable gods were standing at the work, the lesser gods were bearing the toil,
10. The gods were digging the rivers, were piling up the silt (like) *ḫarali*-mineral,
11. The gods were grinding the clay(?), they were putting their life(-breath) into it(?),
12. At that time, the one of broad wisdom, the creator of all the numerous gods—
13. **Enki**, in the deep *engur*, in the subterranean waters, a place no god could look into—
14. Was lying in his sleeping place; from sleep he would not arise.
15. The gods were calling out in tears, making lamentation, saying:
16. "The one who lies sleeping—from his sleeping place he will not arise!"
17. **Namma**, the mother, the foremost one who gave birth to all the numerous gods,
18. Brought the tears of the gods to her son.
19. "You have been lying down... you have been sleeping..."
20. [...] he would not arise
21. "The gods, the creatures of your hands, ... they are bowed down(?)..."

---

This text is part of the **"Enki and Ninmaḫ"** myth, describing the primordial creation and the gods' toil before humans were created to bear their labor.
